findings.title: Missing `prisma` import causes compilation failure
findings.body: The newly added code at line 96 calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but `prisma` is never imported in this file. The imports section (lines 1-20) does not include `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This will cause a TypeScript compilation error and prevent the build from succeeding.

findings.title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with literal placeholder string, corrupting stored credentials
findings.body: When `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` is falsy, it is set to the literal string `"refresh_token"`. This placeholder value will be persisted to the database via `prisma.credential.update` in all callers. On the next token refresh attempt, this invalid string will be sent to the OAuth provider as the refresh token, causing the refresh to fail permanently. The credential becomes unusable until the user re-authenticates.

findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses invalid Zod computed keys that don't create a catch-all
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to a literal string key (the toString representation of a ZodString instance, e.g. something like `"ZodString"`), not a dynamic catch-all index signature. Zod does not support this pattern for passthrough/catchall behavior. The schema will only validate `access_token` and the two literal computed keys, rejecting or ignoring all other properties depending on strictness. The intended behavior should use `.passthrough()` or `.catchall(z.unknown())` on the object schema.

findings.title: Token refresh crashes when credential sharing is enabled because Response object has no `.data` property
findings.body: When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response` object from the sync endpoint. The code then accesses `res?.data` (line 94), but a `Response` object does not have a `.data` property—it needs `.json()` to be called first. This means `token` is `undefined`, and `token.access_token` on line 95 throws a TypeError, breaking all Google Calendar operations for users when credential sharing is enabled.

findings.title: credentialId passed instead of userId to refreshOAuthTokens
findings.body: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is `credentialId` (which is `credential.id`, the credential's database primary key), but the function's parameter is named `userId` and it is sent as `calcomUserId` to the credential sync endpoint. The sync endpoint expects the Cal.com user ID to look up the correct tokens. Passing the credential ID instead means the external system will receive the wrong identifier and likely return incorrect or no tokens.

findings.title: Webhook secret comparison vulnerable to timing attacks
findings.body: The webhook secret is compared using strict inequality (`!==`), which short-circuits on the first differing character. An attacker can measure response times to progressively determine the secret character by character. A constant-time comparison function (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual`) should be used instead.

findings.title: Race condition between findFirst and create/update can produce duplicate credentials
findings.body: The code performs a `findFirst` to check for an existing credential, then conditionally creates or updates it. If two concurrent webhook requests arrive for the same user and app, both may pass the `findFirst` check (finding no existing credential) and both proceed to `create`, resulting in duplicate credential rows. This should use a database-level upsert or a transaction with a unique constraint.

findings.title: Webhook endpoint does not restrict HTTP method
findings.body: The handler function does not check `req.method`, so it accepts GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, and any other HTTP method. A webhook endpoint that creates/updates credentials should only accept POST requests. Allowing GET means the endpoint could be triggered via image tags, link prefetching, or browser preloading, potentially with cached or logged query parameters.

findings.title: Credential sync endpoint called without authentication, exposing user tokens to any network-reachable service
findings.body: The fetch to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no authentication headers, API keys, or signed payloads. If this endpoint is reachable beyond the intended internal network (e.g., misconfigured firewall, exposed on a public IP), any caller can request OAuth tokens for arbitrary users by guessing or enumerating user IDs.

findings.title: Zod parse failure returns unhandled 500 instead of 400
findings.body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a `ZodError` if the request body doesn't match the schema. Since there's no try/catch around this call and no custom error handler, Next.js will return a generic 500 Internal Server Error. The endpoint should catch the ZodError and return a 400 with validation details so callers can diagnose malformed requests.
